policy.action_definition: Rank by (x^T*A_inv*b+alpha*sqrt(x^T*A_inv*x)), multiplied by 1-occurrences/window_size only after agent.t>window_size. x is the host feature vector, A_inv the inverse accumulated feature matrix, b the accumulated credit vector, and occurrences the name's retained agent-history row count.
policy.counter_definition: The native window agent computes rank-aligned current-build reward and replaces each current name's ValueEstimates V with that build credit, defaulting missing joined credit to zero. It still accumulates fractional rank-exposure ActionAttempts N using numpy.linspace(1.0, 1e-12, ranking_length). After incrementing logical observation counter t, it appends every current action row to history with T=t and retains rows with T>max(history.T)-window_size once max(history.T)>window_size. Thus window_size is a number of completed observe/build steps, not rows, pulls or physical time. For every current action with feature column vector x, the contextual policy still adds x*x^T to its matrix A and current-build V*x to vector b, recomputing A_inv=inverse(A). A starts as identity and b as zero for a new/re-entering name. Expired history is not subtracted from A or b. The window only supplies the occurrence discount in the final score; it is not a window-restricted refit. The factory constructs SlidingWindowContextualAgent instances whose score is (x^T*A_inv*b+alpha*sqrt(x^T*A_inv*x))*(1-occurrences/window_size) after agent.t>window_size, without that discount before then. occurrences counts a name's retained history rows. Factory window agents share the same policy matrices, so windows are not independent fits.
policy.guidance: Preserve this explicitly native CI ranking recipe. Generic sampled choice, selected subsets, observed pairwise feedback, calibrated probabilities and independent recipe mixtures need their own qualified implementations; never infer them from this name.

lifecycle.checkpoint_definition: The 37-name mechanical dispatch fixture disabled native restore/checkpoints. No all-policy ordinary pickle or global-RNG recovery guarantee follows.
lifecycle.discovery: Current agent rows drop retired names and append sorted new names; contextual update_actions has its own context setup/re-entry path. No generic identity/version mapping is performed.
lifecycle.reset: Agent.reset zeros current ValueEstimates/ActionAttempts/Q, last ranking and t, but retains action names, policy object/state, agent RNG and caches; window history is not cleared. Environment reset is not fresh construction or RNG rewind.
lifecycle.retirement: Per-name context matrices A, their inverses A_inv and vectors b are retained when agent rows retire. On re-entry, add_action overwrites that name with identity A, inverse identity A_inv and zero b. Context features and feature-list lifetime remain host-owned.
lifecycle.sharing: Factory window agents for one recipe share the SAME policy object; their windows are not independent models or observations.

Inherits A/b accumulation without removing expired sufficient statistics; sliding history discounts final score, not a true window-restricted refit. Multiple windows share same policy matrices.

reward.coverage: Ranking-aligned native learning credit computed from the supplied budgeted metric. Zero for an unscheduled/uncredited position is not evidence of an executed passing test, full observed alternatives or a defined bounded loss. All actual metric/index assumptions remain native.
reward.formula: Per returned ranking position i, emit1 if i+1 is in metric.detection_ranks, otherwise0; when no detection ranks emit an all-zero vector. Rank indices are metric scheduled ranks, not newly observed outcomes.
